result.summary: Independently re-verified REQ-028 (manual check-in list, door, no QR; GitHub issue #31; depends_on REQ-027, REQ-018; first requirement of Phase 6) at commit 07abe27, branch feature/WF02-REQ-028. Did not trust TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 report, the test report yaml, or any prior gate's summary as a substitute for my own re-derivation. 1. Read docs/agents/design/REQ-028.md in full (all 8 sections, AC1-AC6) then read the shipped diff directly (git diff master...HEAD --stat: 25 files, 3251 insertions -- domain/registration.ts's new listAdmittedRegistrantsForCheckin/countCheckedIn/decideCheckinToggleOutcome/toggleCheckIn, handlers/checkin.ts rewritten with makeCheckInHandler + new makeCheckinToggleCallbackHandler/makeCheckinPageCallbackHandler/renderCheckinListMessage, i18n en/ru/types' new checkin.* keys with authorizedStub removed, index.ts's two new bot.callbackQuery registrations, plus the design doc, test spec, ISS-0025, and this run's own handoffs/test-report) and confirmed it matches the design line-for-line: §2.1's SELECT never names profiles.phone/profiles.email and uses the exact displayName derivation table (verified against deriveCheckinDisplayName's if/else chain); §2.2's countCheckedIn is a fresh, uncached count(*) on every call; §3.1's decideCheckinToggleOutcome is the exact first-match-wins table; §3.2's toggleCheckIn opens one transaction, does a FOR UPDATE fresh read, decides, and writes at most one UPDATE + one writeAuditLog call per branch; §4.1-§4.3's handlers match the design's authorization/refusal/re-render sequences exactly, including re-authorization on every toggle (§3.3) and every page turn (§4.3). Confirmed `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts` returns EMPTY -- requireEventStaffForEvent (REQ-018) has zero diff, genuinely unweakened, reused as-is at all three call sites (/checkin entry, toggle, page turn). One minor design-vs-implementation deviation found and assessed non-blocking: design §3.2 step 6 says toggleCheckIn should attach `eventId: row.eventId` 'on every branch where row exists,' but the shipped code's early-return for the refused-not-admitted/not-found branches (`if (row === undefined || (outcome.kind !== "check-in" && outcome.kind !== "undo")) { return outcome; }`) returns before that attachment, so a refused-not-admitted outcome carries no eventId. Verified this has no functional effect: the toggle callback handler (checkin.ts) already resolves its own `eventId` via a separate getEventIdForRegistration call before ever invoking toggleCheckIn (§4.2 step 3's own re-authorization read), and uses that pre-resolved variable -- never outcome.eventId -- for every downstream use including the refusal path. No acceptance criterion or security property depends on outcome.eventId being present on the refusal branch. Flagged for CONTENT/doc-tidiness only, not a defect. 2. Re-ran npm run lint myself: 0 errors, the same 2 pre-existing apps/web LCP warnings (Footer.tsx, Nav.tsx) unrelated to this diff -- matches TEST-RUNNER exactly. Re-ran npm run build myself: apps/web (Next.js/Turbopack) and apps/bot (tsc) both clean. Stood up my own scratch Postgres (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, port 55432; container was already running -- `docker compose up -d` idempotent no-op), ran `DATABASE_URL=... npx drizzle-kit migrate` myself (applied cleanly), then `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` from the repo root: 27 files / 277 tests passed, 0 failed -- matches TEST-RUNNER's count exactly (up from REQ-027's 266-baseline by the reported 11 new REQ-028 cases plus checkin.db.test.ts's contribution). 3. Independent re-verification with my own fresh fixture (apps/bot/scratch-rv-req028.ts, written, run, then deleted -- git status confirmed clean before and after), calling the domain functions directly (listAdmittedRegistrantsForCheckin, toggleCheckIn, countCheckedIn), never reusing BACKEND-DEV's/TEST-DESIGNER's/TEST-RUNNER's committed test files' exact fixtures or tgId bands (own band 991000001-991000004, own chapter/event): - AC1 (write-time recheck): seeded an admitted registration, called toggleCheckIn once to establish a baseline, then flipped that registration's admission to 'withdrawn' by a direct DB UPDATE (simulating an out-of-band admission change between list render and toggle tap, mirroring the design's threat model exactly, not merely re-running the committed test's own page-turn narrative), then called toggleCheckIn again against the now-stale row. Result: outcome.kind === 'refused-not-admitted'; registrations row's checked_in_at/checked_in_by/check_in_method remained null after the call; zero registration.checkin/checkin_undo audit_log rows for that registration -- AC1 independently reproduced, PASS. - AC3 (no phone/email leak): attendee A seeded with a full profiles row (phone +77001234567, email alpha@example.com); attendee B seeded with NO profiles row at all (distinct fixture combination from TEST-RUNNER's, which used a phone/email attendee plus a no-profile attendee too but with different tgId/data values). Serialized the full listAdmittedRegistrantsForCheckin(...) result to JSON and substring-searched for the raw phone and email strings: both absent. B's displayName correctly fell back to the noNameFallback string (no tgUsername either, in my fixture) -- AC3 independently reproduced, PASS. - Concurrent double-toggle (my own Promise.all'd pair, calling toggleCheckIn directly rather than through bot dispatch): two toggleCheckIn calls fired via Promise.all against the identical starting registration (admitted, checked_in_at null). Result: Promise.all resolved without throwing; outcomes were exactly one 'check-in' and one 'undo' (order not assumed); final checked_in_at is exactly null; exactly one audit_log row with action='registration.checkin' and exactly one with action='registration.checkin_undo' for that registration -- matching the READ COMMITTED/row-lock serialization property SECURITY-REVIEWER's and TEST-RUNNER's traces both predicted, independently reproduced with my own fixture, PASS. - AC4 sanity: captured countCheckedIn before and after a direct DB UPDATE setting one more registration's checked_in_at -- count incremented by exactly 1, confirming no cache/stored counter -- PASS. 4. Confirmed full requirement scope: git diff --stat lists only design-doc-listed files (domain/registration.ts, handlers/checkin.ts, handlers/checkin.db.test.ts (new), handlers/checkin.forgery.test.ts (new), i18n/en.ts+ru.ts+types.ts, index.ts, the design doc, the test spec, ISS-0025, and this run's own handoffs/test-report) -- nothing stray. Confirmed authorizedStub is fully removed from types.ts/en.ts/ru.ts with zero remaining references anywhere in apps/bot/src (grep -rn authorizedStub apps/bot/src returns only the removal comment in types.ts). git grep for TODO/FIXME/XXX across the REQ-028 diff: zero matches in actual source (the only 'TODO' substring hits are inside prior handoff-history prose describing a rework, not code). git status --porcelain clean before and after this handoff (my own scratch-rv-req028.ts removed after use). 5. Confirmed requireEventStaffForEvent (REQ-018) is genuinely unweakened: zero diff on domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts (checked in step 1 above), and confirmed by direct read that it is called, unmodified, at all three action points this design specifies (§4.1 step 6, §3.3/§4.2 step 3, §4.3) -- no role short-circuit, no bypass, no relaxed predicate introduced anywhere in this diff. 6. Filed-issue judgment: ISS-0025 (MINOR, filed by TEST-RUNNER this run, spec's own AC1 worked example used unpadded lastName values that would have sorted wrongly) is a test-spec documentation-precision gap already correctly worked around in the shipped implementation and committed test file (zero-padded lastName values used); does not affect shipped correctness. ISS-0013 through ISS-0019 and ISS-0021 through ISS-0024 pre-date this run and are unrelated to REQ-028's surface. ISS-0020 (MAJOR, REQ-018's staff.ts assignment-notification blocked-user gap) is explicitly out of scope per the task context -- it concerns apps/bot/src/handlers/staff.ts's notification send path, a file this diff does not touch at all (confirmed: staff.ts has zero diff in this branch), and REQ-028 introduces no new notification send path of its own (the toggle/page/list handlers only ever reply/edit the acting staff member's own message -- no message is ever sent to the checked-in attendee). None of the filed issues should block this release. Overall: every independent check -- lint, build, the full 277-test suite from the repo root, my own AC1 fixture using a direct DB flip-then-toggle sequence, my own AC3 fixture with a distinct phone/email/no-profile combination, my own concurrent double-toggle Promise.all pair, my own AC4 before/after count comparison, confirmation that domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts and handlers/staff.ts both have literally zero diff -- agrees with all prior gates (CODE-DESIGNER/VALIDATOR, BACKEND-DEV, REVIEWER, SECURITY-REVIEWER, TEST-DESIGNER/VALIDATOR, TEST-RUNNER). No half-implemented scope, no stray TODOs, clean git tree, all design-doc-listed files present. One minor design-vs-code attachment-point deviation (outcome.eventId not set on the refusal branch) found and assessed to have zero functional or security impact, since the handler never reads it on that branch.

issues.description: docs/agents/design/REQ-028.md §3.2 step 6 states toggleCheckIn should attach `eventId: row.eventId` on every branch where the row exists, but the shipped implementation's early-return for the not-found/refused-not-admitted branches returns before that attachment, so those outcomes never carry eventId. Verified no functional or security consequence: the only caller (the toggle callback handler in checkin.ts) already resolves eventId itself via a separate read before calling toggleCheckIn, and never reads outcome.eventId on the refusal path. Recommend a documentation-only correction to the design doc (or a trivial code tweak attaching eventId on the refusal branches too, for future-proofing) on a future pass -- not blocking.
